did_you_know.text: The phrase “You shall not add to it or subtract from it” also appears in Deuteronomy 4:2. It expresses the principle of preserving a command without additions or omissions.
The words “sign” and “wonder” are similar in meaning, but “wonder” usually refers to something especially extraordinary or impressive. In the Bible, they often appear together.

The Sages asked how a person can “cling” to God, and explained it as imitating God’s qualities and practicing kindness. In other words, attachment is expressed through behavior, not only through emotion.
The phrase “the wife of your bosom” is a biblical expression for a deeply loved and close wife. The word “bosom” refers to the chest and arms, creating an image of intimacy and closeness.
“Worthless men” is a biblical expression for wicked or lawless people. In the Bible, “Belial” is not necessarily the name of a specific person, but a term for corrupt behavior.

In this chapter, the word “ḥerem” means more than a prohibition: it refers to something completely devoted to destruction under religious law. “An everlasting ruin” means a heap of ruins that will never be rebuilt.
